recent.text: With Paulo Rauber and David Ledvinka, I am starting the project [Enabling the analysis of stochastic algorithms in Lean](https://www.renaissancephilanthropy.org/enabling-the-analysis-of-stochastic-algorithms-in-lean), supported by the [AI for Math Fund](https://www.renaissancephilanthropy.org/ai-for-math-fund) of Renaissance Philanthropy. It develops the tools to write, run and analyze randomized algorithms in Lean, so that humans and AI systems can prove statistical guarantees about algorithms that run on real data.

I co-authored the blog post [How to Formalize All of Mathematics](https://xenaproject.wordpress.com/2026/10/16/how-to-formalize-all-of-mathematics/), with {{Jeremy Avigad}}, {{Kevin Buzzard}}, {{Johan Commelin}}, {{Kim Morrison}}, {{Oliver Nash}} and {{Adam Topaz}}.
I am giving a tutorial at ICML 2026 on Proving Theorems with Lean and Machine Learning, with {{Wenda Li}}.

I organized the [Lean Together 2026](https://leanprover-community.github.io/lt2026/) online conference, the annual meeting for users, developers, and fans of the Lean programming language and theorem prover and its library Mathlib.

I gave talks about probability theory in Lean and the Brownian motion project at [ItaLean 2025](https://pitmonticone.github.io/ItaLean2025/) (Bologna, Italy, December 9-12), a workshop about bridging formal mathematics and AI.

With {{Michael Rothgang}}, I am leading a [workshop on Lean for PDEs](https://www.slmath.org/workshops/1180) at the Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute (SLMath), co-organized by the new Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics (ICARM).

I am launching the [FORMAL Inria exploratory action](https://www.inria.fr/index%2ephp/fr/formal). Its goal is to formalize bandit and reinforcement learning algorithms and their theory in the Lean theorem prover. A post-doc will join the team in 2026 to work on this project.

I am contributing to the formalization of the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture in Lean. This is a project led by Terence Tao, who recently proved this result with W. T. Gowers, Ben Green and Freddie Manners. See [this post on Terence Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2023/11/18/formalizing-the-proof-of-pfr-in-lean4-using-blueprint-a-short-tour/) for a tour of the project.

older.text: I am looking for a post-doc who would join the [Inria Scool team](https://team.inria.fr/scool/) and work on bandits and sequential testing (Position filled).
I was awarded an ANR JCJC funding for my project FATE (Frugal and adaptive testing). This project will fund a PhD and a post-doc on bandits and sequential testing.

I co-organize the [**Complex Feedback in Online Learning**](https://cfol-workshop.github.io/) workshop at ICML 2022 (Baltimore, July 23). This workshop aims to present a broad overview of the feedback types being actively researched in sequential learning (reinforcement learning, bandits, games...), highlight recent advances and provide a networking forum for researchers and practitioners.
